__NOTOC__

This page is the interface between Emma (human) and the bot agents that work on this wiki. Agents post open questions and blockers here when they hit a decision that requires human judgement. Emma answers them on the wiki. Agents read the wiki version each session and act on the answers.

== How to use this page ==

* '''Agents:''' when you hit a blocker (a design call, a credential need, a wiki-side action you cannot take, an ambiguous instruction), add it under the relevant section below with enough context that Emma can answer without re-deriving the problem. Don't move items out of "blocked" sections on your own — wait for Emma's edit on the wiki.
* '''Emma:''' edit answers in-line under each question. When you've answered a question and the agents have acted on it, strike or delete the question. Free-form notes that don't fit anywhere else go under [[#Notes|Notes]] below.
* '''This page is different from other git-synced pages.''' The wiki is the canonical source of truth here. When Emma edits this page on shinto.miraheze.org, those edits should propagate down to the repo (wiki-wins for this page). Agents must not silently overwrite Emma's wiki edits with stale repo content. The current default <code>git_synced/</code> conflict policy is repo-wins; for this page specifically, agents should treat the wiki as authoritative until the broader revision-aware conflict-resolution refactor lands. See [[#Sync-policy exception note|the policy note]] at the bottom.

== Currently open ==

=== Shintowiki bot pipeline (`shintowiki-scripts` queue) ===

* '''Cloud-queue consumer still uses a cursor.''' The claude.ai scheduled routine that drains <code>remote_queue.json</code> walks <code>consume_remote_queue.state</code> in order. Emma wants statefulness to be purely file-presence + category — each run should scan <code>duplicated_content/</code> for files still tagged <code>[[Category:Pages with duplicated content]]</code> and pick at random. The routine's prompt defines this and can't be edited from the repo. ''Needs:'' Emma to reword the routine via claude.ai/code/routines (trigger id <code>trig_013F9aeKeL3hx8zo7weKj3Ed</code>).
* '''Kana ojp-hani manual stragglers.''' Items with 0 or >1 ojp-hani P1448 official name surface in the <code>seed_kana_qualifier.py --dry-run</code> "AMBIGUOUS" report (e.g. Q135040786 with no ojp-hani name). ''Needs:'' Emma handles these directly on Wikidata as they appear; no bot action.
* '''Sync conflict resolution should be revision-aware, not static policy.''' Currently per memory: wiki-wins for duplicated_content / need_translation; repo-wins for git_synced / fandom_unique / miraheze_unique. Emma's stated rule: whichever side is further ahead in revisions wins, with per-directory tie-break rules (TBD). ''Needs:'' Emma to specify the per-directory tie-break rules so the sync scripts can be rewritten.
* '''<code>delete_lowercase_template_collisions.py --apply</code> is blocked.'''  The 19 lowercase <code>Template:Infobox <name></code> case-collision twins on both shintowiki and shinto.fandom.com can't be deleted yet — every lowercase variant still has live transclusions, so the script's safety gate refuses. ''Needs:'' the <code>canonicalize_template_case</code> op (wired into all 12 orchestrators) to finish its sweep across every namespace so the transclusions all point at the canonical capitalised form; then re-run the deleter with <code>--apply</code>. No human action required, just CI cycles.

== Sync-policy exception note ==

By default, files in <code>git_synced/</code> use repo-wins conflict resolution (per <code>feedback_sync_conflict_policy.md</code> in the bot's memory). This page is intended to be edited primarily ON the wiki by Emma. Until the revision-aware conflict-resolution refactor lands (see the queue item above), agents working on <code>shintowiki-scripts</code> should:

# Always pull this page from the wiki at the start of a session (don't trust the repo copy alone).
# When committing changes to other files, never include a stale repo version of this page in a sync push.
# If you're about to edit this file in the repo, first confirm the wiki version hasn't been updated since the last sync — otherwise you'd clobber Emma's answers.
